fluff.overview:
The Athena Combat Vehicle is a 75-ton tracked fire-support platform developed by Clan Hell's Horses at the Niles Industriplex Alpha on their Homeworld of Niles. Entering production in 3008, the design embodies the Horses' longstanding and unorthodox preference for conventional armored vehicles in roles that most Clans reserve exclusively for BattleMechs. Conceived to bring Clan-grade accuracy and hitting power to a vehicle chassis, the Athena can threaten enemy BattleMechs at extreme range and does so reliably enough that it earned comparison to some of the most dangerous Clan OmniMechs in terms of firepower delivery.

Though its defensive characteristics are more modest than those of Inner Sphere vehicles of equivalent tonnage, the Athena compensates through combined-arms doctrine, always operating under BattleMech or Elemental cover. Its unusual success has drawn quiet admiration even from Clans skeptical of conventional vehicle forces, and the design has spread through capture and salvage to several other Clans over the decades since its introduction.
fluff.capabilities:
The Athena functions as a dedicated long-range sniper platform built around twin Type AA4 Gauss rifles fixed in the forward hull compartment. Mounting these weapons in the hull rather than a rotating turret sacrifices traverse flexibility, but provides exceptional stability for accurate fire at extreme range. A Type Xa LRM-10 rack extends the vehicle's reach for indirect fire missions. A secondary semi-independent turret mounts two Series 2h Extended Range Medium Lasers and two Type AP40 Machine Guns, crewed by a secondary gunner whose primary duty is keeping lighter threats at bay while the main crew concentrates on priority targets.

The critical performance multiplier is the Consolidated Type VII targeting computer paired with a Mark-5 Series Targeting Enhancement module. This system equals those carried by frontline Clan OmniMechs and allows even average crews to place Gauss slugs on the most vulnerable sections of enemy armor at distances most vehicles cannot reach. The design's weaknesses are equally clear. Ground speed is sufficient only to keep pace with the heaviest assault elements, and the ferro-fibrous armor protection is particularly weaker than Inner Sphere vehicles of the same tonnage. The secondary gunner is typically the crew's lowest-ranked warrior, reflecting the Athena's primary mission emphasis on long-range fire over close-quarters defense.
fluff.deployment: The Athena serves in the heavy and assault vehicle Stars of nearly every frontline Cluster and Galaxy in Clan Hell's Horses. Horses command considers these vehicles too valuable to risk in unsupported operations, and crews rarely deploy without accompanying BattleMech or Elemental elements. In assault operations they anchor the long-range fire component, engaging priority targets while faster elements close distance. Salvaged examples appear in limited numbers with Clan Wolf and Clan Jade Falcon, typically integrated into vehicle Stars rather than used as standalone assets.
fluff.history:
The Athena's development grew directly from Clan Hell's Horses' doctrinal commitment to conventional armor at a time when nearly all other Clans viewed vehicles as supplementary assets at best. The Horses' leadership recognized that a vehicle chassis capable of delivering Clan-grade firepower with OmniMech-level accuracy could serve their combined-arms formations as effectively as a dedicated BattleMech at a fraction of the resource cost. Design work at Niles Industriplex Alpha produced a functional prototype by the early 31st century, and the Athena entered series production in 3008.

Over the following decades, the Athena became a cornerstone of Hell's Horses armor doctrine, serving in heavy and assault vehicle Stars across nearly every frontline Cluster. The design's combat record was tested severely during the Jihad, when Clan Ghost Bear contested the Horses' Homeworld holdings. During the battle for Niles Industriplex Alpha, a Trinary of freshly manufactured Athenas attached to Alpha Galaxy proved decisive, crippling nearly two full BattleMech Binaries of Ghost Bear forces and helping blunt the Bears' advance on the facility.

Despite this success, the broader disruption of the Jihad severed reliable contact with the Niles production line. Beginning around 3072, Swedenborg Heavy Industries on the Inner Sphere world of Kirchbach began producing the standard Athena under license, initially at comparatively low cost. The Horses used this accessibility to push the design into second-line units as part of their post-Jihad rebuilding program. For a time, the Horses even attempted to market the vehicle to other interested parties, and Clan Wolf, Clan Jade Falcon, and others acquired examples through both purchase and battlefield capture. By the Dark Age, Swedenborg Heavy Industries represented the primary active production source for the design, keeping the Athena in service with Hell's Horses through the ilClan era.
